title: Google Sheets `COUNTIF`: a `?` or `*` in the criterion is a WILDCARD — use `~?` to count a literal question mark
summary: COUNTIF criteria treat ? as any single character and * as any run of characters. Counting cells equal to "Why?" also counts "Why!" and "Whys". Prefix the character with a tilde (~) to match it literally.
body_markdown:
## The trap
- `=COUNTIF(A:A, "Why?")` counts `Why?`, `Why!` and `Whys`: `?` matches any single character.
- It bites when the criterion comes from data: a cell reference such as `COUNTIF(A:A, B2)`, where B2 holds a user's text.

## Fix
- Escape wildcards in the criterion: `"Why~?"`.
- When the criterion comes from data, escape it first: replace `~` with `~~`, `?` with `~?`, and `*` with `~*` (in that order), for example with nested `SUBSTITUTE` calls.

sources.title: Google Sheets COUNTIF
sources.note: Criterion can contain wildcards: ? for any single character, * for zero or more; prefix with ~ to match them literally.
